# Step 1: Review and serve your order

## Read the real order

This is an explicit, staff-assigned, real GitHub-connected pilot. It is unranked. Stay inside this canvas and read the assigned exercise issue and drink criteria. Staff prepared the PR; no Copilot authorship is asserted.

## Inspect the proposal

Open Summary, Changes, and Checks in order above. These are real GitHub details for the pinned PR revision, not simulated fixtures or native App views. Each open records in-canvas observation only. It does not prove comprehension or qualify for the event leaderboard.

Compare the name, price, serving style, artwork, description, and one-drink scope with the order. Check that the displayed required checks passed. If verification fails, current review progress is cleared; ask staff to restore the original assignment, then inspect again.

## Check the order

Submit your own price, serving style, and change-scope answers. The checkpoint compares those answers with the catalog and freshly verified GitHub change. Use hints freely; this pilot has no score.

If an answer does not match, follow Return to Changes to compare your answer and try again. Do not approve until the facts match.

## Decide, then verify serving

Only choose Approve pull request if you intend to submit a real GitHub approval. The canvas verifies the designated reviewer, exact revision, current checks, and your checkpoint. Approval is not merge and never changes the menu by itself.

A separately authorized operator or workflow must merge the PR without bypassing branch protection. Choose Verify merged menu afterward. Pending merge leaves the order approved, not served. Retry verification in the same run when the merge is ready.

## Read your unranked app result

Your app result and House menu show the independently verified merge and menu. Pilot learning finished is not native Skills completion or event finalization. There is no generated handle, score, rank, QR, AI judge, leaderboard submission, or final exercise-issue update.

Inspect, check, approve: you compared the proposed change with the order before making a human review decision. There is no next learner step.
